wantToLearn: Become a better manager for my team
whyText: I was promoted to lead my team of five engineers three months ago. My 1:1s feel aimless and I avoid hard feedback.

approach.approachNotes: Managing well is mostly a set of conversations done deliberately, not a personality trait. The leverage right now is two things: giving your 1:1s a real structure so they stop feeling aimless, and saying the hard thing earlier and smaller, before it becomes a big thing. Skip frameworks about org design for now — you don't have that problem yet. Practice on real conversations this week, not hypothetical ones.
approach.practice: A short scripted move you try in your next real 1:1 or feedback moment, then a quick page reviewing how it landed.
goodLooksLike: 1:1s have a recurring structure the engineer can anticipate and prepare for.
You name a specific behavior and its impact within a day of noticing it.
Engineers bring you problems before they're emergencies.
pitfalls: Mistaking being liked for being trusted — avoiding feedback feels kind but reads as disengagement.
Treating 1:1s as status updates instead of the person's own agenda.
Vague feedback ('be more proactive') that gives no actionable next step.
progressionPrinciples: Start with 1:1 structure and small corrective feedback before tackling performance issues or conflict.
Practice one specific phrasing or move at a time, not general 'communication skills.'
Move from scripted language to adapting tone once the basic moves feel natural.

successOutcomes: I run 1:1s my engineers look forward to
I give hard feedback within a day, calmly
